sourcedFrom: IWI TAVOR® 7 Semi-Automatic Rifle 7.62X51mm Operator Manual — 08.011.01.17.00 (2022)
cleanIntro: The 7.62X51 Tavor 7 is its own rifle with its own book — a CHARGING handle that wedges in a notch, a four-position adjustable gas regulator with a removable piston, and a bolt group that comes apart on a firing pin securing pin and a bolt leader pin. Nothing here transfers from the SAR or the X95, and the gas system is the part that makes the post-firing clean worth doing properly.

steps.title: Safety to SAFE, magazine out, stock in the shoulder
steps.action: Thumb the safety lever to SAFE, press the magazine release lever and pull the magazine down and out. Hold the grip with your strong hand, trigger finger straight on the frame, and keep the stock in your shoulder with the muzzle pointed somewhere safe while you work. On a bullpup in .308 the chamber is a few inches from your jaw, so the safety goes on before the charging handle is touched.
steps.aside: Press the magazine release lever and pull the magazine down and out of the rifle.
steps.quote: Using your thumb, ensure that the safety lever is positioned to “SAFE”
steps.cite: IWI TAVOR® 7 Semi-Automatic Rifle 7.62X51mm Operator Manual — 08.011.01.17.00 — 6.1.1 Unloading and Safety Check, step 1, printed p.28 (PDF page 30)

steps.title: Charging handle cycled three times, hard
steps.action: Cycle the bolt by pulling the charging handle fully back three times, releasing it each time so the carrier runs home under spring pressure. Do not ride it forward. A .308 case sitting in the chamber needs a carrier at full speed to be caught by the extractor and thrown out; a hand-walked carrier will leave it sitting there and you will call the rifle clear when it is not.
steps.quote: Cycle the bolt by pulling back on the charging handle fully three times releasing the charging handle to let the bolt carrier move forcefully each time (do not “RIDE” the charging handle forward).
steps.cite: IWI TAVOR® 7 Semi-Automatic Rifle 7.62X51mm Operator Manual — 08.011.01.17.00 — 6.1.1 Unloading and Safety Check, step 5, printed p.28 (PDF page 30)

steps.title: Charging handle wedged in its notch to hold the bolt back
steps.action: Lean forward, roll the rifle so the butt is horizontal with its right side uppermost and brace it. Pull the charging handle to the rear and RAISE it until it wedges in the charging handle notch at the rear of the slot. That is how the Tavor 7 holds its bolt open — there is no bolt carrier stop lever to press as there is on the SAR and X95, and the handle is released later by pushing DOWN on it.
steps.aside: Push downward on the charging handle to release the bolt.
steps.quote: Pull the charging handle to the rear and raise the handle until it is wedged in the charging handle notch at the rear of the slot.
steps.cite: IWI TAVOR® 7 Semi-Automatic Rifle 7.62X51mm Operator Manual — 08.011.01.17.00 — 6.1.1 Unloading and Safety Check, step 6, printed p.28 (PDF page 30)

steps.title: Muzzle down 45°, chamber looked at, hammer dropped
steps.action: Lower the muzzle forty-five degrees below horizontal and look into the chamber, with a flashlight if the light is poor. When it is confirmed empty, push down on the charging handle to release the bolt, lower the muzzle again, move the lever to FIRE and press the trigger to drop the hammer, then put the lever back to SAFE.
steps.quote: Check visually that the chamber is empty (“CLEAR”).
steps.cite: IWI TAVOR® 7 Semi-Automatic Rifle 7.62X51mm Operator Manual — 08.011.01.17.00 — 6.1.1 Unloading and Safety Check, step 8, printed p.28 (PDF page 30)
steps.warn: You must not “think” the chamber is empty, you must KNOW it is empty, because if you are wrong, death or serious injury may result.

steps.title: Butt plate locking pin across, recoil mechanism out the back
steps.action: Push the butt PLATE locking pin from the right with a punch or a bullet tip and draw it across to the left until it stops. It is captive; leave it in the rifle. Open the butt plate and pull the recoil mechanism straight out of the rear — carrier, bolt, firing pin and spring all together. Unlike the Tavor SAR, the Tavor 7 has no sear-removal precondition on this step.
steps.aside: Pull the recoil mechanism (3) out of the rifle.
steps.quote: Push the butt plate locking pin (1) with a punch or bullet tip on the right side and pull it through the rifle to the left side until it stops. DO NOT PULL THE PIN OUT COMPLETELY.
steps.cite: IWI TAVOR® 7 Semi-Automatic Rifle 7.62X51mm Operator Manual — 08.011.01.17.00 — 7.1.1 Recoil Mechanism, Removal, step 1, printed p.36 (PDF page 38)
steps.warn: Be sure the rifle is unloaded before starting the disassembly!

steps.title: Gas regulator rotated round to its initial position and lifted off
steps.action: With the recoil mechanism already out, put a 7.62X51mm round or a punch into the opening on the gas regulator and rotate it CLOCKWISE through the settings until it reaches its initial position. The securing spring drops into the regulator recess at that point and the regulator is free. Slide the regulator and the piston assembly off the regulator base together, then separate them.
steps.aside: Slide gas regulator (1) together with piston assembly (4) off regulator base (3) (c).
steps.quote: Insert a 7.62X51mm round or a punch into the opening on the gas regulator (1) and rotate through the gas settings clockwise until the gas regulator (1) reaches its initial position (a).
steps.cite: IWI TAVOR® 7 Semi-Automatic Rifle 7.62X51mm Operator Manual — 08.011.01.17.00 — 7.2.1 Gas Regulator and Piston Assembly, Removal, step 1, printed p.38 (PDF page 40)
steps.warn: With gas regulator (1) and piston assembly (2) removed, the piston rod is not supported inside the rifle body and may fall out.

steps.title: Firing pin securing pin opened, firing pin unit out
steps.action: Take a 3 mm punch to the firing pin securing pin on the RIGHT side of the recoil mechanism and push it to the open position. It stays connected — do not drive it out. With it open, draw the firing pin unit out of the bolt carrier. Note the C-pin arrangement: on reassembly both the securing pin and the C pin sit between the flanges of the firing pin.
steps.aside: Extract the firing pin unit (2) from the bolt carrier.
steps.quote: Using a 3 mm punch, push the firing pin securing pin (1) (connected) on the right side of the assembly to the open position (1a).
steps.cite: IWI TAVOR® 7 Semi-Automatic Rifle 7.62X51mm Operator Manual — 08.011.01.17.00 — 7.6.1.1 Recoil Mechanism, Disassembly, step 1, printed p.46 (PDF page 48)

steps.title: Bolt leader pin out, bolt assembly out — spring stays on the pin
steps.action: Extract the bolt leader pin from the carrier and take the bolt assembly out. That is as far as this goes: IWI's step 3 says in capitals not to take the firing pin spring off the firing pin. The pin and spring are handled as one unit for cleaning, and on the way back the bolt goes in with the extractor on the RIGHT — the ejection side.
steps.caution: Do NOT remove the firing pin spring (6) from the firing pin (5).
steps.aside: Install the bolt assembly (4) inside the bolt carrier. Make sure the extractor is on the right (ejection) side.
steps.quote: Extract the bolt leader pin (3) from the bolt carrier and remove the bolt assembly (4).
steps.cite: IWI TAVOR® 7 Semi-Automatic Rifle 7.62X51mm Operator Manual — 08.011.01.17.00 — 7.6.1.1 Recoil Mechanism, Disassembly, step 3, printed p.46 (PDF page 48)

steps.title: Sear mechanism out — storage clean only, not every strip
steps.action: For a post-firing clean the Tavor 7 book leaves the sear alone; it comes out only for the Cleaning Gun for Storage routine. Press the two locking pins from the right and draw them through to the left until they stop, open the bolt carrier stop lever, and pull the sear mechanism out. With it out of the rifle the hammer must not be released — nothing supports it and it will damage the housing. It goes back in CHARGED.
steps.caution: Do not release the hammer when the sear mechanism is removed from the rifle. This will damage the housing.
steps.aside: Pull sear mechanism (3) out of the rifle.
steps.quote: Press the two locking pins (1) on the right side and pull them through the rifle to the left side until they stop. DO NOT PULL THE LOCKING PINS OUT COMPLETELY.
steps.cite: IWI TAVOR® 7 Semi-Automatic Rifle 7.62X51mm Operator Manual — 08.011.01.17.00 — 7.3.1 Sear Mechanism, Removal, step 1, printed p.40 (PDF page 42)

steps.title: Field strip complete — the book stops you here
steps.action: Recoil mechanism out and broken into bolt, firing pin unit and carrier; gas regulator and piston off; sear mechanism out if you are cleaning for storage. That is the whole published operator-level strip. Section 7 ends with a STOP, and the reason given is not only the warranty — IWI names unsafe conditions that could result in death or serious injury.
steps.quote: Further disassembly by individuals who are not factory-trained and certified as TAVOR® 7 armorers can result in damage to or destruction of the rifle, voiding of the warranty, and possibly the creation of UNSAFE CONDITIONS THAT COULD RESULT IN DEATH OR SERIOUS INJURY.
steps.cite: IWI TAVOR® 7 Semi-Automatic Rifle 7.62X51mm Operator Manual — 08.011.01.17.00 — STOP! / CAUTION! closing section 7, printed p.49 (PDF page 51)

deepAbsentReason: The Tavor 7 book's cleaning content is two routines — 9 Maintenance (Pre-Firing and Post-Firing, printed pp.51-52) and 10 Cleaning Gun for Storage (printed pp.53-54) — and between them they call for exactly four removals: the recoil mechanism, the gas regulator and piston, the recoil mechanism's own secondary disassembly, and for storage the sear mechanism. All four are walked above, so a deep branch would only repeat them. The only other disassembly the book publishes at operator level is 7.4 Hand Grip Assembly, 7.5 Foregrip Assembly and 7.6.2 Foregrip Assembly secondary disassembly, none of which the cleaning routines call for; and section 7 closes with a STOP against going further unless you are a factory-trained and certified TAVOR 7 armorer. Section 8 is an exploded view — a parts drawing, not a procedure — and nothing was constructed from it.

cleaning.name: BARREL & CHAMBER
tasks: Pass the cleaning rod with a cleaning patch through the barrel, always starting from the chamber end towards the muzzle
Use the brass barrel bore brush and let it clear the muzzle before pulling back, several times
Use the chamber and barrel extension brush on the chamber and the locking lugs of the barrel extension

cleaning.name: GAS REGULATOR & PISTON
tasks: Scrub the carbon off the regulator, from under the securing spring, and from the piston rings area
Leave the regulator and the piston clean and DRY — this is the one area the manual says not to oil
Check the piston rod is in place before the regulator and piston go back on

cleaning.name: RECOIL MECHANISM
tasks: Clean the recoil mechanism parts thoroughly and inspect them for cracks and fractures
Use a high quality gun oil on the bolt, the bolt leader pin, and the contact surfaces between bolt carrier and body insert
Verify the extractor and ejector springiness once it is back together

cleaning.name: BODY & SEAR (STORAGE CLEAN)
tasks: Clean the exterior body with the general cleaning brush and the interior with the internal receiver brush
Clean the metal surfaces of the sear mechanism with the general cleaning brush
With the hammer charged, lightly lubricate the hammer spring coils
For long storage, re-clean and re-lubricate regularly and remove the excess oil before firing

reassembly: Install the bolt assembly inside the bolt carrier with the extractor on the right (ejection) side, then fit the bolt leader pin.
Install the firing pin unit into the bolt carrier and close it with the firing pin securing pin behind the unit; the securing pin and the C pin sit between the firing pin's flanges.
Check the piston rod is in place, insert the piston assembly into the gas regulator, align the regulator's smooth side with the surface of the regulator base and slide it to the initial position.
Rotate the gas regulator COUNTER-clockwise with a 7.62X51mm round until it locks into the setting you want — R regular, A adverse, S suppressed, O off.
Slide the recoil mechanism forward into the body through the rear, close the butt plate and press its locking pin home.
If the sear mechanism was out, place it in the body with the hammer CHARGED, close the bolt carrier stop lever and push both locking pins fully in.
fncheck: Run the manual's Function Test before the rifle is handled as ready: inspect it and verify it is assembled properly; pull the charging handle to the rear and release it and verify free movement of the bolt assembly; on SAFE, press the trigger and confirm the hammer does not fall; set FIRE and press the trigger until the hammer releases; then cycle, press and hold the trigger, cycle again, let the trigger forward until you hear the reset, and confirm the hammer releases; finally insert an empty magazine and confirm the magazine catch holds it. Return the gas regulator to position I (regular) — the manual states the rifle should not be run in position II (adverse) for an extended period.
